why: Then-vs-now city reels are one of the most shared transition formats; Pakistani cities and landmarks get huge local engagement and proud shares.

series.name: Then & Now: Pakistan
series.style: photorealistic cinematic look, same famous view of the place in every picture, golden-hour light, high detail, vertical 9:16 frame
series.negative: text, letters, words, watermark, logo, real people, celebrities, blood, blurry, distorted
rules: Same place, same camera angle in every stage; only the era changes.
Labels are eras or years that are well known (e.g. 1900s, 1947, Today). Never invent exact dates.
Old eras look like aged photographs with warm sepia; today looks bright and modern.

topics: Lahore Fort and the Badshahi Mosque view from the 1600s to today
Karachi Saddar and Empress Market from the 1890s to today
Islamabad: from empty Margalla foothills in the 1950s to the Faisal Mosque city of today
Peshawar Qissa Khwani Bazaar through the centuries to today
Gwadar: from a small fishing village to a modern port city
Murree Mall Road from the 1900s hill station to today
Faisalabad Clock Tower and its eight bazaars from the 1900s to today
Multan: the city of shrines and blue tiles through the ages
Hunza valley: from an old mountain village to today's tourist valley
Minar-e-Pakistan site from 1940 to today's park
